diagnostic_evidence.quote: with $\lambda_i u_i = 0$ and $\mu_i(u_i - C_{k(i)}) = 0$ such that

issues.failure_explanation: With the stated pairing ($\lambda_i$ the multiplier of the lower bound $u_i=0$, $\mu_i$ that of $u_i \le C_{k(i)}$, both $\ge 0$), correct stationarity for this QP is $G_i = -s_i\rho + \lambda_i - \mu_i$, i.e. $G_i - s_i\rho = \lambda_i - \mu_i$. The displayed equation has the opposite right-hand side. Applied at a variable at its lower bound ($\mu_i = 0$, $\lambda_i \ge 0$) it yields $G_i \le \rho$, i.e. $\tau_k \ge -\rho$ for $\alpha_k = 0$, whereas Table 1 and the true KKT conditions ($\alpha_k = 0 \iff y_k - f(x_k) \le y_k\varepsilon/100 \iff \tau_k \le b = -\rho$) require $\tau_k \le -\rho$; every bound-state inequality comes out reversed.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Flip the sign of the right-hand side, writing $G_i - s_i\rho = \lambda_i - \mu_i$ (equivalently swap the $\lambda/\mu$ roles in the complementary-slackness sentence); Table 1 and all downstream content then follow unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The KKT characterization in Section 3 is internally inconsistent: the displayed stationarity yields the opposite inequalities to the paper's own Table 1. Since Table 1 (used for working-set selection and bias recovery) is the mathematically correct statement, no downstream result is invalidated, but the section's central displayed equation is false as written.
issues.title: KKT stationarity equation has flipped multiplier signs, contradicting Table 1
issues.why_classification: A one-line sign repair (RHS order or multiplier pairing) restores full consistency; no substantive claim, guarantee, or labelled result depends on the erroneous form.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
The optimal threshold $-\rho$ lies in the interval
$[\tau_{j^*}, \tau_{i^*}]$ (from~\eqref{eq:mvp} and Table~\ref{tab:kkt}).

issues.failure_explanation: By the paper's own Table 1, at an optimal solution every $i \in \Iup$ (i.e. $\alpha_k = 0$, free, or $\alpha_k^* = C_k$) satisfies $\tau_i \le -\rho$ and every $j \in \Idown$ satisfies $\tau_j \ge -\rho$; hence $\tau_{i^*} = \max_{\Iup}\tau \le -\rho \le \min_{\Idown}\tau = \tau_{j^*}$, the opposite of the displayed chain $\tau_{i^*} \ge -\rho \ge \tau_{j^*}$. Counterexample: with $\Omega = I_2$, $y = (1,2)$, $\varepsilon \approx 0$, $C_k = 0.2$, the optimum $\alpha = (0, 0.2)$, $\alpha^* = (0.2, 0)$ has $\Iup = \{1, 3\}$ with $\tau_{i^*} = 1.2$ and $\Idown = \{2, 4\}$ with $\tau_{j^*} = 1.8$, and every optimal bias $b = -\rho$ lies in $[1.2, 1.8]$; the displayed chain demands $1.2 \ge -\rho \ge 1.8$, which no optimal point satisfies. The error only manifests when $\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{free}} = \emptyset$ (then $\tau_{i^*} \le -\rho \le \tau_{j^*}$ with possibly strict gaps), exactly the case the remark addresses; with free support vectors both sides collapse to equality and the error is masked. The midpoint estimator $\hat b = (\tau_{i^*}+\tau_{j^*})/2$ is unaffected since it is symmetric in the two endpoints.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reverse the two inequalities to $\tau_{i^*} \le -\rho \le \tau_{j^*}$ (and, in Section 7, state the optimality bracket as $[-\rho \in [\tau_{i^*}, \tau_{j^*}]]$ at convergence); no other change is needed.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed KKT bracket for the bias when $\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{free}} = \emptyset$ is false (correct relation: $\tau_{i^*} \le -\rho \le \tau_{j^*}$); the same reversed orientation appears in Section 7's interval claim. The midpoint convention, the algorithm, and all guarantees remain valid.
issues.title: Optimal-threshold bracket reversed in the no-free-SV bias bound
issues.why_classification: A two-sign local repair restores a correct statement; the midpoint convention, the algorithm, and every advertised guarantee survive unchanged, so no mathematical content is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
If
$\Delta^{\mathrm{full}} > \varepsilon_{\mathrm{tol}}$, a frozen variable
violates KKT: reset $\Aactive = \{1,\ldots,N\}$, $\Afrozen = \emptyset$,
update $\tau$ from~\eqref{eq:reconstruct}, and continue.  Otherwise, the
solution is certified optimal.

Finite termination to $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tol}}$-optimality follows
from standard results~\cite{Fan2005, Chang2011}.

issues.failure_explanation: The reconstruction/verification block is placed after \EndFor, and the branch $\Delta^{\mathrm{full}} > \varepsilon_{\mathrm{tol}}$ executes 'Reset $\Aactive$; continue outer loop' — but no outer loop exists in the procedure. Executed as written, the algorithm falls through the reset branch directly to the bias computation and \Return, so when unshrinking reveals that a frozen variable violates KKT ($\Delta^{\mathrm{full}} > \varepsilon_{\mathrm{tol}}$) it returns a solution that is not $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tol}}$-optimal instead of resuming optimization as Section 7.3 specifies ('reset ... and continue. Otherwise, the solution is certified optimal'). The stated guarantee of finite termination to $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tol}}$-optimality for the complete procedure therefore fails on this branch.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Wrap the SMO loop together with the reconstruction/verification block in an outer repeat-until-$\Delta^{\mathrm{full}} \le \varepsilon_{\mathrm{tol}}$ loop governed by a global iteration budget; the reset branch then resumes optimization as intended. This is the standard LIBSVM-style structure and requires no new mathematics.
issues.overall_effect: The complete algorithm does not deliver its advertised certified $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tol}}$-optimality whenever shrinking was applied and a frozen variable violates KKT at reconstruction; the returned dual variables and bias can be non-optimal. The per-iteration mathematics and all other branches are unaffected.
issues.title: Algorithm 1 never re-enters optimization after the unshrinking reset
issues.why_classification: A local control-flow repair (wrapping the existing loop and check in an outer loop with a global iteration budget) preserves every substantive claim and guarantee; no new lemma, construction, or argument is required.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
For the symmetric-kernel
variant (m2) with $a = +1$, $P \succeq 0$ is preserved and the same
guarantees apply.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims the m2 dual is convex for $a = +1$ because $\Omega$ and $\Omega^*$ are individually PSD. The premise is false: $\Omega^*_{k\ell} = K(\mathbf{x}_k, -\mathbf{x}_\ell)$ is a cross-Gram between the training points and their reflections, which is in general neither symmetric nor PSD — already for the paper's RBF kernel with a training set containing a reflected pair ($x_1 = 1$, $x_2 = -1$ gives $\Omega^* = [[e^{-4\gamma}, 1],[1, e^{-4\gamma}]]$ with eigenvalue $e^{-4\gamma}-1 < 0$). The conclusion itself also fails for general PSD kernels: for the valid PSD kernel $K(x,x') = 1 + xx' + (x+x^2)(x'+x'^2)$ (feature map $\varphi(t) = (1, t, t+t^2)$) with points $\{1, -3\}$, $\Omega_s = \tfrac12(\Omega + \Omega^*)$ is not even symmetric and its symmetric part $\left[\begin{smallmatrix}3&13\\13&55\end{smallmatrix}\right]$ is indefinite, so the m2 dual QP is not convex. The claim is true only for reflection-invariant kernels such as the RBF, where $\Omega_s$ is the Gram matrix of the even features $\tfrac12(\varphi(x)+\varphi(-x))$; the paper neither states this hypothesis nor supplies this argument, so the m2 $a=+1$ convexity/convergence guarantee is unsupported as written.

failure_location.quote:
For $a = +1$ (even symmetry), $\Omega_s \succeq 0$
follows from the fact that $\Omega$ and $\Omega^*$ are individually PSD.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the missing hypothesis (e.g., reflection-exchange kernels such as the RBF, for which $\Omega_s$ is the Gram matrix of the even features $\tfrac12(\varphi(x)+\varphi(-x))$ and hence PSD) and prove $\Omega_s \succeq 0$ from it; or weaken the advertised m2 $a=+1$ convergence claim to that kernel class.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised guarantee that Algorithm 1 applies to m2 with $a = +1$ with the same convexity and convergence guarantees is unsupported as written and false for general kernels; only reflection-invariant kernels (e.g., the RBF) are covered. The m1 results and the m2 $a=-1$ caveat are unaffected.
issues.title: m2 claim that $\Omega_s \succeq 0$ for $a=+1$ is unjustified and false in general
issues.why_classification: The repair requires a new, contained nontrivial argument (even/odd feature symmetrization) plus an explicit hypothesis, but the advertised m2 $a=+1$ guarantee survives for the kernels the paper actually uses (RBF), so no advertised regime is abandoned — more than minor, less than serious.
